title: Bright v. Bechtel Petroleum, Inc. (1986)
summary: The court rejected an attempt to keep a federal tax-withholding dispute outside federal court by labeling it a contract claim.
notes:
The syllabus abbreviates the case as “Bechtel.” The assigned note is short.

Bright filed a W-4 claiming exemption from federal income-tax withholding and then sued in California state court for breach of contract when Bechtel withheld anyway; Bechtel removed, the district court denied remand, dismissed, and awarded attorney's fees, and the Ninth Circuit affirmed and imposed sanctions for a frivolous appeal, invoking the artful-pleading doctrine as a limit on the plaintiff's status as master of the complaint.

sections.Parties: An employee sued Bechtel over amounts withheld from wages.
sections.Material Facts: The complaint used a state-law contract theory to challenge withholding that implicated federal tax requirements. The jurisdictional dispute concerned whether the pleading’s chosen label accurately described the legal basis of the controversy.
sections.Procedural History: The Ninth Circuit sustained the removal treatment described in the casebook’s artful-pleading discussion.
sections.Issue: Could the plaintiff defeat removal merely by describing the tax-withholding challenge as a contract action?
sections.Holding: No, under the court’s analysis of the actual nature of this claim.
sections.Reasoning: The court looked beyond the label to the federal legal requirements that the claim sought to challenge. The note illustrates an exception to taking the plaintiff’s characterization at face value. It should remain tied to its particular context: ordinary federal defenses to contract claims remain insufficient under Mottley, and the presence of any federal ingredient does not justify removal.

learning.why: The court rejected an attempt to keep a federal tax-withholding dispute outside federal court by labeling it a contract claim.

topics.cp-removal: The court treated the wage-withholding claim as a disguised challenge concerning federal tax requirements. A state-law label did not control the court’s analysis of the actual claim.
topics.cp-well-pleaded: Artful pleading is the recognized exception to the well-pleaded complaint rule that the case applies.
topics.cp-federal-question: The court recharacterized the contract claim as one necessarily arising under federal tax law.
topics.cp-certification: The Ninth Circuit imposed sanctions for a frivolous appeal and affirmed a fee award.

mnemonic.rationale: A W-4 claiming exemption from withholding
